correctness.rationale: The proof first classifies all dominating 2-sets as the n deleted-matching pairs. For each such pair, a deleted edge destroys it exactly when the edge's two indices include that pair index. Because edge deletion cannot create a new dominating pair, raising domination above 2 is equivalent to covering all indices. Inclusion-exclusion then gives the full polynomial, and minimum covers give the bondage number and multiplicities. A standalone exhaustive checker independently reconstructs adjacency, enumerates all base dominating pairs, and checks every edge-deletion subset for n=3,4,5; coefficient identities are also checked through n=12. No finite computation is used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Bondage measures robustness of a minimum domination structure under link failures. The finding gives more than the scalar threshold: it classifies every disrupting edge set by a clean no-isolated-vertex condition and supplies the full failure-size enumerator. The reduction to edge covers of K_n exposes a structural reason for the parity-sensitive minimum counts and yields an immediately reusable exact reliability profile for a classical symmetric network family. This is not a mere substitution into a known complete-multipartite formula because deleting the defining perfect matching changes both the minimum dominating sets and the edge-failure incidence structure.
